rows.why: Clock time takes the feminine number (el-saa3a wa7de); he said واحد and then said 'dates are واحد, times are واحدة' right after her chat - her voice is missing here, so the cue is inferred.

rows.medi_said: Oh, الـ سيارة، uh, or سيارة الـ B... No, it's double noun. Oh, سيارة الـ BMW.
rows.why: First word of an idafa never takes el- and grows -t (sayyaaret el-BM); he put الـ on سيارة while working it out after her (inaudible) correction of his 09:49 'الBMW', she typed sayyaaret el-BM illi.

rows.amal_said: Yes, but what's work bag without any my or yours?
rows.why: In idafa the owner ending goes on the last word, not the first: he started Shanteti, she prompted 'work bag without any my', he then said 'Shantet Shogoli, not Shanteti Shogoli'.
Shantet shu8li is definite, so the adjective after it needs el-; without it it means 'is red', as Amal explained.

rows.medi_said: So would it be شنتت، شنتت شغلي الأحمر، الأحمر،
rows.why: شنتة is feminine so the adjective must be el-7amra; she recast الحمرا and typed shantet shu8li el-7amra.

rows.amal_said: Not here. ... ما فيهن means there aren't here
rows.why: ma fihon means 'there aren't here'; 'not here' uses mish before the adverb: mish hon (she said مشون and typed mish hon).
He added the feminine -t to اسم (a masculine noun); Amal said no, it's just اسم, it can't be feminine.
'That's how I knew it' from a male speaker: feminine participle عارفة + ها; masculine would be 3aarefha (about اسم, masc). Amal let it pass; participles not taught yet.
A noun with a possessive ending is definite and takes no el-; her chat esem madrasto shows no el-, but she only said Mm-hmm (could be a hesitation الـ).
The first word of an idafa never takes el-; she said لا twice (29:57, 30:21) to الـ اسم.

rows.medi_said: So الـ اسم قديم. No, it's like اسم القديمة. Okay, I don't know.

Before the noun taani is the tool word 'second'; ishi taani (after) is 'something else'; she corrected his reading twice.
